nodes.label: mock-throttle deployment (429 -> api_throttle)
nodes.rationale: mock_response carries the sentinel string 'litellm.RateLimitError', which litellm's /v1/messages route recognises and raises as a REAL exception carrying status 429 -- the status classify_exclusion maps to the pre-registered reason api_throttle.

nodes.label: mock-5xx deployment (500 -> api_5xx)
nodes.rationale: Raises litellm.InternalServerError at status 500, which classify_exclusion maps to api_5xx.

nodes.label: mock_response sentinel exceptions
nodes.rationale: The error deployments raise REAL exceptions, not canned error bodies. Verified in litellm 1.95.0 (llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/utils.py): three sentinel strings are recognised on the /v1/messages route and raise the corresponding litellm exception carrying the status code classify_exclusion maps to a reason. RateLimitError 429 -> api_throttle, InternalServerError 500 -> api_5xx, ContextWindowExceededError 400 -> not an infra failure by design. There is no sentinel for Timeout (408), so that branch stays unit-tested -- stated rather than left as an apparent gap. Answering from mock_response is what lets the whole capture path run with no credentials and no spend, because a gate that costs money is a gate that stops being run.

nodes.label: num_retries: 0 in the fault-injection config
nodes.rationale: Deliberately unlike production. A retry would turn one injected 429 into four wire entries and make the test assert on retry behaviour instead of on capture. The retry-versus-final-error rule is covered by its own unit test.

nodes.label: router_settings.disable_cooldowns (fault injection)
nodes.rationale: Verbatim copy of the production rationale, so the gate exercises the same router behaviour it certifies.
